mode: compile_only — authorization + approval + audit design; no rendering, no send, no clone execution authorized; no activation authorized
category_definition: AI drafts/renders a voice message in the authorizing operator's own explicitly-authorized voice, intended for delivery to another person. This is the HIGHEST-RISK voice category. Nothing in this packet renders audio, sends a message, or executes a voice model — it is the governance-and-consent design only.

activation_gate.note: This artifact DESIGNS a governed mutation and an authorization/approval model. It authorizes none of it. No mutation is registered in mutation_registry.py by this packet.

hard_requirements.note: These five are BINDING and HARD. No downstream packet may weaken, remove, or make optional any of them. Each is phrased as a hard requirement (MUST / never / prohibited).

HR1_approval_before_send.requirement: The authorizing operator's explicit approval is REQUIRED before ANY external send. This is a HELD gate, never an auto-send. Rendering produces a HELD artifact that sits at AWAITING_APPROVAL; the system MUST NOT transmit to any recipient until the operator explicitly approves that specific rendered message.
HR1_approval_before_send.phrasing: MUST have explicit operator approval before any external send; a held gate; never auto-send

HR2_full_audit_trail.requirement: A full proof/audit trail is REQUIRED for every rendered message: who authorized the voice, under which grant, what text was rendered, which voice model/provider was used, who approved the send, when, to whom (recipient identity), and the disclosure applied. The audit record MUST be created before send and MUST be immutable after.
HR2_full_audit_trail.phrasing: MUST maintain a full proof/audit trail for every render and every send

HR3_no_covert_impersonation.requirement: NO covert impersonation. Every outbound AI-rendered voice message MUST carry a recipient-facing disclosure that it was AI-rendered in the authorizing operator's voice. Sending an AI-rendered voice message that the recipient would reasonably believe is a live human recording, without disclosure, is PROHIBITED.
HR3_no_covert_impersonation.phrasing: no covert impersonation; recipient-facing disclosure is mandatory

HR4_no_third_party_cloning.requirement: NO third-party voice cloning. ONLY the authorizing operator's OWN voice may be modeled, and ONLY with an explicit, recorded VoiceAuthorizationGrant for that voice model. Cloning, rendering, or sending in any other person's voice is PROHIBITED with no exception.
HR4_no_third_party_cloning.phrasing: no third-party voice cloning; only the operator's own explicitly-authorized voice

HR5_external_send_is_high_risk_governed_.requirement: External send is a HIGH-risk governed mutation with EXTERNAL blast radius and require_approval=true. It MUST route through the canonical governed spine (governed_mutation). There is no ungoverned or direct send path.
HR5_external_send_is_high_risk_governed_.phrasing: external send MUST be a high-risk, EXTERNAL-blast-radius, approval-required governed mutation

voice_authorization_model.description: The authorizing operator authorizes use of THEIR OWN voice. This is distinct from send approval: authorization licenses the existence and use of the voice model; send approval gates each individual outbound message.

VoiceAuthorizationGrant.description: A recorded, revocable, per-purpose consent that the authorizing operator's own voice may be modeled and used to render outbound messages. Design-only shape; nothing here creates one.

fields.authorizing_principal: resolved server-side (authenticated Clerk principal) — never a hardcoded literal; the operator who OWNS the voice being authorized
fields.voice_model_ref: opaque reference to the authorized voice model artifact (never raw model bytes in this record)
fields.self_voice_attestation: bool — MUST be true; attests the voice being authorized is the authorizing principal's OWN voice (HR4)
fields.purpose_scope: enum/list — per-purpose scope for which rendering is authorized (e.g. outbound_voice_message); authorization is NOT blanket
fields.consent_recorded_at: ISO-8601 UTC — when the authorizing operator granted
fields.consent_evidence_ref: reference to the recorded consent/authorization evidence (how the operator expressed authorization)
fields.revocable: const true — the grant is always revocable
fields.revoked_at: ISO-8601 UTC | null — once set, all rendering and sending under this grant is refused fail-closed
fields.expires_at: ISO-8601 UTC | null — optional bounded lifetime

invariants: self_voice_attestation MUST be true — a grant for any voice other than the authorizing principal's own is invalid (HR4)
revocation is immediate and fail-closed: after revoked_at, no render and no send may proceed under this grant
authorization is per-purpose, never blanket — a grant scoped to one purpose does not authorize another
the grant licenses the voice model's use; it is NOT a send approval — each outbound message still requires HR1 send approval
identity is resolved server-side; the authorizing_principal is never stamped from client input

third_party_cloning_prohibition.statement: Third-party voice cloning is PROHIBITED. Only the authorizing operator's own voice, under a VoiceAuthorizationGrant with self_voice_attestation=true, may be modeled or rendered. There is no code path, flag, or mode in this design that renders another person's voice.
third_party_cloning_prohibition.enforcement_design: render precondition checks self_voice_attestation=true on a live (non-revoked, non-expired, purpose-matching) grant; absence or falsity fails closed with no render

approval_gate.description: The held-gate lifecycle. Render never sends. Send is the operator's explicit act.
approval_gate.flow: authorize (VoiceAuthorizationGrant) -> render_requested -> rendering -> rendered_held (AWAITING_APPROVAL) -> operator explicitly approves -> proof recorded -> send (governed mutation) -> sent; OR operator rejects -> rejected (no send, no trace to recipient)
rules: render produces a HELD artifact at AWAITING_APPROVAL — rendering NEVER sends (HR1)
no message reaches any recipient until the authorizing operator explicitly approves that specific rendered artifact (HR1)
auto_send is not a field, not a mode, and MUST NEVER be added — there is no auto-send path (HR1)
approval is per-message: approving one rendered artifact never pre-approves the next
reject or revoke from any pre-sent state discards the rendered artifact and produces NO outbound send
the send step is the governed mutation (ai_outbound_voice_send) — the gate is enforced by the spine, not by UI alone (HR5)

held_gate.no_auto_advance: MUST NOT auto-advance past awaiting_approval; only an explicit operator approval decision advances it (HR1)

audit_proof_trail.description: The shape of the required proof/audit trail (HR2). Every render and every send appends an immutable record.

fields.grant_id: vag-<id> — the VoiceAuthorizationGrant the render ran under
fields.authorizing_principal: server-resolved principal who owns the voice
fields.approving_principal: server-resolved principal who approved the send (HR1) — recorded, never client-stamped
fields.voice_model_ref: which voice model rendered the audio
fields.provider: which TTS/voice provider executed the render (design placeholder; provider creds via 1Password per HR/credential law)
fields.rendered_text: the exact text rendered to speech (retained for audit; treated as operator data)
fields.recipient_identity: who the message was addressed to — required in the record before send (HR2)
fields.disclosure_applied: the recipient-facing AI-voice disclosure that was attached (HR3)
fields.audio_artifact_ref: pointer to the rendered audio (tenant/session-scoped, authenticated retrieval; bytes never logged)

invariants: an AiOutboundVoiceProofRecord MUST exist before any send is permitted (HR2)
the record is immutable after write — append-only audit, never edited in place
recipient_identity and disclosure_applied are REQUIRED fields on any record whose decision is 'approved' (HR2, HR3)
audio bytes and any provider secrets are never written into the proof record or logs — only references

audit_proof_trail.logging_law: audio bytes never logged; rendered_text never logged at INFO (<=40-char DEBUG previews only, mirroring the voice storage law); provider credentials never logged

anti_impersonation_disclosure_policy.description: Recipient-facing disclosure is mandatory (HR3). This specifies what disclosure means and when it applies.
anti_impersonation_disclosure_policy.policy: Every outbound AI-rendered voice message MUST be accompanied by a recipient-facing disclosure that the audio was AI-rendered in the authorizing operator's voice. The disclosure is part of the message payload, not an optional add-on.
disclosure_channels: in-message audio preamble or trailing statement, and/or
accompanying text/caption on the message delivery surface
requirements: no covert impersonation: an AI-rendered message MUST NEVER be delivered in a way a reasonable recipient would take as a live human recording without the disclosure (HR3)
the exact disclosure applied is recorded in the proof trail (disclosure_applied) before send (HR2, HR3)
if the delivery surface cannot carry the disclosure, the send is refused fail-closed — no disclosure, no send

governed_mutation_design.note: DESIGN ONLY. This mutation is NOT registered in mutation_registry.py by this packet. Registering it, wiring it, or executing it is out of scope and forbidden here.

spec_design.name: ai_outbound_voice_send
spec_design.allowed_modes_design: ASSISTED only — never AUTONOMOUS; a human approval is structurally required (HR1)
spec_design.description: Send an AI-rendered outbound voice message (rendered in the authorizing operator's own authorized voice) to an external recipient — approval-required, EXTERNAL blast radius, high risk; the held gate is enforced by the governed spine
rationale: risk_level=high + blast_radius=external + require_approval=true encode HR5 and HR1 at the spine level
degraded_mode_allowed=false: this MUST NEVER execute when the control plane is down (fail closed) — unlike low-risk local mutations
irreversible: an external send cannot be recalled, which is exactly why the held approval gate precedes it

governed_mutation_design.entrypoint_design: governed_mutation(mutation_name='ai_outbound_voice_send', intent=..., execute_fn=<send>, source='cockpit', require_approval=True, verification_fn=<disclosure+grant+proof present>, metadata={grant_id, render_id, recipient, disclosure}) — illustrative shape only; not called by this packet
not_done_here: no MutationSpec constant added to substrate/organism/mutation_registry.py
no route handler, no execute_fn, no provider call

requirements: any TTS/voice-provider credentials (API keys, tokens) flow through 1Password — resolved via `op run --env-file=<tpl>` with op:// URIs, never hardcoded, never plaintext CLI args, never committed
provider credentials never appear in the proof record, logs, artifact metadata, or the JSON of this design
voice model artifacts and provider secrets are referenced, never inlined
validate_credential_source() (substrate/execution/credential_gate.py) is the substrate check to call before any authenticated provider use — design reference; not invoked here

threat_model.description: What could go wrong and which gate prevents it. Every threat maps to a hard requirement.

threats.threat: Covert impersonation — recipient believes a live human sent the audio
threats.prevented_by: HR3 mandatory recipient-facing disclosure; disclosure recorded in proof before send; no disclosure => no send

threats.threat: Third-party voice cloning — someone else's voice is modeled/rendered
threats.prevented_by: HR4 self_voice_attestation=true precondition on a live grant; no render path for non-self voices

threats.threat: Auto-send / accidental blast — a rendered message goes out without human review
threats.prevented_by: HR1 held gate at awaiting_approval; no auto_send field/mode; per-message explicit approval; HR5 spine-enforced require_approval

threats.threat: Ungoverned or degraded-mode send when the control plane is down
threats.prevented_by: HR5 governed mutation with degraded_mode_allowed=false — fails closed, no send

threats.threat: Credential leak — provider API key exposed in logs/records/CLI
threats.prevented_by: Credential Injection Law: 1Password op run injection; secrets never logged or inlined

threats.threat: Repudiation — no record of who authorized/approved/sent what to whom
threats.prevented_by: HR2 immutable AiOutboundVoiceProofRecord created before send with authorizing + approving principal, recipient, disclosure

threats.threat: Scope creep — a blanket grant used for unauthorized purposes
threats.prevented_by: per-purpose VoiceAuthorizationGrant; purpose_scope checked at render; revocable and expirable

rollback.description: Because this is compile-only, rollback is primarily documentary; the design's own rollback for a future implementation is included.
rollback.compile_rollback: revert the three artifacts (this JSON, docs/AI_OUTBOUND_VOICE_COMPILE.md, the test) — nothing is wired, so removal is a clean git revert with zero runtime effect
future_implementation_rollback_design: grant revocation: set revoked_at on the VoiceAuthorizationGrant — immediately refuses all render and send fail-closed
feature flag off: the ai_outbound_voice_send mutation, once (in a future authorized packet) registered, can be gated behind a flag whose off-state means no render, no send
no recall of already-sent audio is possible (external, irreversible) — which is why HR1's held gate is the real protection, not rollback

forbidden_in_this_packet: sending any message to any recipient
executing or training any voice model / clone
writing any projection or live DB
weakening, removing, or making optional any of HR1–HR5
